title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned the Server Rack for your backend engineer portfolio. Keep it, take the Status Console (Impeccable's pick), an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Server Rack
options.lineage: the datacenter rack: servers, patch panels, status LEDs, cable runs
options.thesis: Every project is a unit in a running rack — backend infrastructure made legible, the systems you've built shown the way an operator sees them.
options.viewport: A three-rack cabinet fills the hero: each project is a rack unit with an engraved nameplate and status LEDs for live / demo / source; the featured unit sits with its panel swung open, its latch in safety yellow.

raised.raise: Line-by-line pour-in reveal: headings arrive one line at a time, terminal-slow, the page's one signature motion.
One severity condition bar: the featured project carries the only alarm-like element on the page, a bar that fills across the collection.
Mixed-size engraved headlines: section titles set like wood type — a shouting line above supporting lines, in relief.
Nested status outlines, grain-locked: availability (shipped, in-progress, screens-only) renders as solid-vs-dashed outlines that never leave the alignment grid.

Staged case-study process: every project page moves through deliberate stages (overview → problem → solution → architecture → challenges → result), each result carrying a still map of what exists — live, demo, source, or screens only.

options.risk: A hardware theme is one step from cliché unless the panel stays honest: real statuses, real labels, and warmth in the copy — not decorative LEDs.

options.label: The Status Console
options.lineage: the NOC status board: uptime, service health, error budgets
options.thesis: The portfolio as an operations status board: every project is a service under monitoring, and "all systems nominal" is the proof of the work.
options.viewport: A status wall: the hero is a service table where each project row shows a green operational dot, and the featured project's row carries the only anomaly — a short incident log that resolves to resolved.
options.risk: Familiar: the dark-console-with-neon status look is the default developer-portfolio move; it wins only with discipline and real content.
options.case: Holds both audiences instantly — recruiters and clients both read "systems stay up" — but it is the most common category move.

options.label: The Nixie Counter
options.thesis: Numbers as glowing tubes — experience, project counts, uptime as physical digits that change by cross-fading depth.
options.viewport: A bank of nixie tubes in the hero: each milestone a digit position, the featured metric lit orange while the rest sit dark in their envelopes.
options.case: Holds precision-instrument appeal engineers feel on sight, but numbers alone cannot carry case studies; loses on product clarity to the rack's structure.
options.risk: Metrics-first risk: reduces the work to counts and makes depth hard to show.

options.label: The category standard
options.thesis: What this category ships — dark hero, code window, card grid, tech tags — executed impeccably.
options.viewport: The arrangement every developer-portfolio visitor expects, at full craft.
options.risk: Indistinguishable from the competition by design.

options.label: The ANSI Nightboard
options.thesis: A dial-up BBS: the portfolio as a numbered text menu, one caller at a time.
options.case: Retro-nostalgia identifies engineers but reads hobbyist to clients; a text menu buries the case studies.
options.kept: Line-by-line pour-in reveal — headings arrive one line at a time, the page's one signature motion.

options.label: The Crisis Wall
options.thesis: A crisis wall: hazard chevrons, seven-segment countdowns, red condition bars.
options.case: Reads as game UI, which the brief bans; "crisis" actively fights the "reliable business systems" claim.
options.kept: One severity condition bar for the featured project — the single alarm-like element on the page.

options.label: The Calavera Broadside
options.thesis: A penny-press newsprint sheet: shouting wood-type headline, two hard columns of verse.
options.case: Print craft charms, but skeleton engravings and verse columns do not signal software depth.
options.kept: Mixed-size wood-type headlines — section titles with one shouting line in relief.

options.label: The Pattern Envelope
options.lineage: home sewing pattern envelopes and tissue
options.thesis: A pattern envelope and tissue: view letters A/B/C, nested dashed cut lines, grain arrows.
options.case: Variant and nesting discipline maps well to responsive and status states, but dressmaking misidentifies the trade.
options.kept: Nested status outlines, grain-locked — availability as solid-vs-dashed outlines that never leave the grid.

options.label: The Raku Vessel
options.thesis: A raku vessel fired through stages: fire, expose, cover, cool, reveal — a black-white skin from process.
options.case: Process-as-stages is a strong case-study shape, but ceramics as the world misleads a business audience.
options.kept: Staged case-study process — every project moves through deliberate stages with a still map of each result.
